subject: Fitting spatial model with two SPDEs

messages.author: a9cd27d9c6c4baa9
messages.subject: Fitting spatial model with two SPDEs
parts:
Hello!
I am trying to fit a spatial model using two spatial fields. In essence, I am assuming that there are two underlying spatial "states", and each year in my dataset is a linear combination of these two states. A crude representation of what I want to do would be:

formula <- obs ~ -1 +  
year : f(spatial.field1, model = spde1_mod4) +
year : f(spatial.field2, model = spde2_mod4)

Though I am aware that I cannot specify the interaction like this. I'm not sure if I can use the 'group' argument, since I don't want the actual spatial field to vary between years, just an overall coefficient that will be applied to the entire spatial field. Is there a way to implement this in R-INLA?

Thank you!!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting spatial model with two SPDEs
parts:
As far as I understand you, then you have replicated measurement of the two
fields over years, then you could write them as

a * field.1 + (1-a) * field.2
or
s * ( \sqrt{a} * field.1 + \sqrt{(1-a)} * field.2) (*)

as you see, then the variances of field.1 and 2 are confounded with 'a', hence
this can be achived with

field.1 + field.2

and the 'a' follows from the variances. the (*) representation would require
that the variances of field.1 and 2 are fixed, like = 1, then s^2 is the overall
variances, and 'a' in (*) is the variance particion. (see
https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16057 for a recent treatment of variance particion)

messages.author: a9cd27d9c6c4baa9
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting spatial model with two SPDEs
parts:
Hello again,
I think I was able to come up with a solution (albeit not a very elegant one). I fit a joint likelihood model where each year has a separate formula:
obs_y1 = intercept + spatial.field1 + spatial.field2
obs_y2 = intercept + beta_sf1y2 * spatial.field1 + beta_sf2y2 * spatial.field2
...
obs_yn = intercept + beta_sf2yn * spatial.field1 + beta_sf2yn * spatial.field2

where the effect in bold is specified as f(spatial.field1.n, copy = spatial.field1, hyper = list(beta = list(fixed = FALSE)))

To my understanding, this copies the effect of spatial.field1 (with a small error) and allows for estimation of the beta (which is what I had wanted).

This seems to run ok, although as you predicted the model is struggling to differentiate the two spatial processes. I am still figuring out how best to inform the priors but thought I'd share what I've done so far in case you have any thoughts.

Thank you for all the help!
